item.title: The residual map as a stratified fibration over the resonance arrangement
item.author: Dawei Chen, Scott Mullane, Nick Salter, Guillaume Tahar
item.description:
Dawei Chen, Scott Mullane, Nick Salter, Guillaume Tahar

Matched: Dawei Chen · math.GT, math.AG · cross

Given a stratum $\mathcal{H}(\mu)$ of meromorphic one-forms on a Riemann surface with prescribed orders of zeros and poles, the residual map assigns to each differential the collection of its residues at the poles. In this paper, we prove that the residual map is a locally trivial topological fibration over each open flat of the stratification induced by the resonance arrangement. To give an algebro-geometric proof of this result, we introduce a refined compactification of the projectivized stratum $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{H}(\mu)$, namely the moduli space of residue-aligned multi-scale differentials $\operatorname{RAMS}(\mu)$. We prove that the projectivized residual map extends to $\operatorname{RAMS}(\mu)$ as a stratified fibration over the projectivized resonance arrangement, thereby yielding a resolution of the projectivized residual map. This approach naturally extends to the analogue of the residual map for strata of $k$-differentials. Complementing the algebro-geometric approach, we also develop a flat-geometric point of view. In genus zero, each isoresidual fiber carries a canonical higher-dimensional analogue of a translation structure. These fibers admit a metric completion whose boundary has a modular interpretation in terms of the WYSIWYG compactification, for which we provide explicit local models. Isoresidual fibers admit a polyhedral cell decomposition whose geometry varies linearly with the underlying configuration of residues in period coordinates. Degenerations of these cells occur precisely when resonance conditions are satisfied, providing a geometric proof that the residual map is a stratified fibration. Finally, certain isoresidual fibers admit natural interpretations as Hurwitz spaces of branched covers, yielding unexpected homeomorphisms between moduli spaces of covers with prescribed ramification profiles.

item.title: On rational curves relative to a divisor
item.author: Jiun-Cheng Chen, Hsian-Hua Tseng
item.description:
Jiun-Cheng Chen, Hsian-Hua Tseng

Matched: Hsian-Hua Tseng · math.AG · new

Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and $D$ a reduced simple normal crossings divisor. We prove that, given a complete curve of negative $(K_X+D)$-degree, through its general points there is a rational curve whose normalization meets $D$ in at most one point. The proof uses ordinary weighted jets of a smooth family constructed from $(X,D)$, a positive parameter line bundle, and an intersection calculation on a ruled surface. We obtain an explicit degree bound depending on a projective embedding. We apply this construction to a cyclic cover compactification associated with a smooth Campana orbifold $(X,\sum_i(1-1/m_i)D_i)$. If its anticanonical divisor is big, we show that there is a covering family of free divisible Campana rational curves with fixed numerical class and contact data. In Picard number one case, the orbifold is Campana rationally connected.

item.title: The super Weil-Petersson asymptotic expansion and the coefficients
item.author: Xuanyu Huang, Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu
item.description:
Xuanyu Huang, Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.AG, math-ph, math.DG, math.MP · cross

We determine the universal constant in the large-genus asymptotic expansion of super Weil-Petersson volumes. The argument adopts the uniform-transport strategy for shifted theta intersection numbers. The uniform large-genus theorem for normalized BGW numbers of Guo-Norbury-Yang-Zagier determines the amplitude at a simpler endpoint. The result is $C=\pi^{-9/2}$. We give a proof of the Griguolo-Papalini-Russo-Seminara conjecture for fixed boundary lengths and fixed descendant degrees. The boundary formula is uniform when the sum of the lengths is $o(\sqrt g)$, and we exhibit an obstruction at the $\sqrt g$ scale. We also compute the first four inverse-genus coefficients by two exact recursive methods and derive general polynomial structure results. Finally, we show that, for each fixed genus, the super Weil-Petersson volume divided by $n!$ is a polynomial in the number $n$ of marked points.

item.title: Algebraicity, Hodge Gradings, and the Geometry of Period Images
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Yang Shen
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Yang Shen

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.AG · new

We prove the algebraicity of period images in arithmetic quotients without using o-minimality. The proof uses infinitesimal neighborhoods and formal algebraization to recover the images and the maps from their algebraic sources. Hodge positivity and an algebraic ampleness criterion yield the Griffiths polarization and quasi-projectivity. For lifted images, we construct Stein neighborhoods and holomorphic matrix realizations of the Hodge filtration. On closed horizontal subspaces, we bound canonical Bergman density below by the Hodge volume form. We compare the Bergman and Griffiths--Schmid metrics near one-parameter boundaries with nontrivial unipotent monodromy and nondegenerate graded period maps, and in all directions near general one- and two-node quintic threefolds. A period surface arising from abelian threefolds shows that the upper metric comparison fails in general.

item.title: Fibrewise Real-Analytic Landsberg Metrics in Dimension at Least Four Are Berwald
item.author: Ming Li, Kefeng Liu
item.description:
Ming Li, Kefeng Liu

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.DG · new

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge4$, and let $F$ be a smooth, strongly convex Landsberg metric, regular on the entire slit tangent bundle. We prove that $F$ is Berwald if, at each fixed base point, the Minkowski norm is real-analytic on the entire slit tangent space. The proof rests on two analytic rigidity theorems for a single Minkowski space. The first asserts that, in dimension at least $3$, a real-analytic Minkowski norm whose Hessian metric is flat is induced by an inner product. The second asserts that, in dimension at least $4$, the Hessian metric of a real-analytic Minkowski norm is flat if the entire indicatrix carries a nonzero smooth symmetric quartic form satisfying a twisted Codazzi equation. The quartic form need not be real-analytic, and the second theorem is proved independently of the first. Applying these results to the angular Berwald quartic form shows that the metric is Riemannian on the open set of base points on whose fibres the Berwald curvature is not identically zero. Since every Riemannian metric is Berwald, this set must be empty. No analytic structure, compactness or completeness of the base manifold is assumed, and the metric need not be reversible.

item.title: 5d SCFTs and Intersection Theory of Generalized Toric Threefolds
item.author: H\"ulya Arg\"uz, Antoine Bourget, Pierrick Bousseau, Julius F. Grimminger, Sakura Schafer-Nameki
item.description:
H\"ulya Arg\"uz, Antoine Bourget, Pierrick Bousseau, Julius F. Grimminger, Sakura Schafer-Nameki

Matched: Pierrick Bousseau · hep-th · new

Five-dimensional superconformal field theories are intrinsically strongly coupled fixed points that can be realized as M-theory on local Calabi-Yau threefolds with canonical singularities. The low-energy effective theory on their extended Coulomb branch is governed by a cubic prepotential, determined by the triple intersection numbers of divisors in the resolved geometry. For toric threefolds, dual to 5-brane webs, these numbers are computed combinatorially from the toric polygon. However, no such description has been available for generalized toric polygons (GTPs), dual to 5-brane webs with 7-branes, since the corresponding generalized toric Calabi-Yau threefolds are generally non-toric. We show that the 7-brane data are encoded by additional lines in the GTP, which correspond to non-toric, non-compact divisors that we call exuberant divisors. Building on a local analysis of these divisors and on the associativity of the intersection product, we develop an algorithm that computes the triple intersection numbers, and hence the prepotential, directly from the combinatorial data of the GTP. We illustrate it in examples and provide a Mathematica code implementation of the intersection algorithm.

item.title: Canonical quantum curve I
item.author: Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang
item.description:
Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang

Matched: Shuai Guo · math-ph, math.AG, math.MP · new

We formulate a canonical quantum curve conjecture $\widehat H\Psi_*=0$ for spectral curves of positive genus. Here $\Psi_*$ is the non-perturbative wave function associated with Eynard--Orantin topological recursion, specialized at the \emph{canonical vanishing point}, a distinguished zero of the closed non-perturbative partition function. The operator $\widehat H$ is obtained by Weyl quantization of $H(x,y)$, with $\widehat x=x\cdot$ and $\widehat y=\hbar\partial_x$, together with quantum corrections to its coefficients. These corrections depend only on closed moduli and $\hbar$ and vanish classically. Whenever a geometric definition is available, we conjecture that the corrected coefficients are suitably normalized Wilson-loop expectation values. When a corresponding refined theory exists, we conjecture a relation between the canonical vanishing point and the closed Nekrasov--Shatashvili free energy. We prove the quantum curve conjecture for Weierstrass curves and the mirror curves of canonical bundles of smooth projective toric weak del Pezzo surfaces, including local $\mathbb P^2$. For the local surfaces considered here, we relate the canonical vanishing point to a derivative of the closed NS free energy. For local $\mathbb P^2$, we also identify the corrected coefficient with a suitably normalized, geometrically defined NS Wilson-loop expectation value.

item.title: Gromov-Witten theory of the local model of the standard flop
item.author: Alex D\"anzer, Yannik Schuler
item.description:
Alex D\"anzer, Yannik Schuler

Matched: Yannik Schuler · math.AG · new

We conjecture that the generating series of equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of the local Calabi-Yau $(2n-1)$-fold $\operatorname{Tot} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{n-1}} (-1)^{\oplus n}$ at fixed genus can be presented as a linear combination of polylogarithms, generalising a well-known property of the resolved conifold. We prove this conjecture for two specialisations of the equivariant parameters. In the first, the parameters are specialised to roots of unity and the proof proceeds via Givental-Teleman reconstruction. In the second, we obtain a closed-form evaluation of the generating series from which the conjecture follows. For $n=3$, the resulting closed formula establishes a special case of a Gopakumar-Vafa-type conjecture for Calabi-Yau fivefolds.

item.title: The Coxeter-Todd abelian sixfold, Gamma00, and big Schottky
item.author: Samuel Grushevsky
item.description:
Samuel Grushevsky

Matched: Samuel Grushevsky · math.AG · new

We recall the construction of the Coxeter-Todd principally polarized abelian sixfold, and study its special properties. We show that the base locus of the Gamma00 linear system on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold consists of 253 points, disproving the stronger version by Donagi and Beauville--Debarre of the Gamma00 conjecture of van Geemen and van der Geer. This also leads us to construct explicit indecomposable 7-dimensional principally polarized abelian varieties that are not Jacobians, but lie in the so-called Big Schottky locus, thus disproving the corresponding conjecture from the Schottky-Jung approach to the Schottky problem. We furthermore show that while no even theta constant vanishes for the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, its associated Scorza quartic is identically zero. Finally, we show that there exist two different theta level (2,4) structures on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, for which the sets of second order theta constants are projectively equal. This disproves the expected injectivity of the second order theta constant map for all genera starting with 6.

item.title: A proof of the spectral rigidity for complex projective space
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.DG · new

We give a proof of a folklore conjecture that a compact K\"ahler manifold with the same scalar Laplace spectrum as complex projective space equipped with the Fubini--Study metric is holomorphically isometric to it. More generally, we prove that the spectrum of the Hodge Laplacian in any one fixed degree $p$ determines $\CP^n$ up to holomorphic isometry among compact connected K\"ahler manifolds, for every fixed pair of integers $(p,n)$ with $0\leq p\leq n$. Equality of a single Hodge spectrum first forces periodic geodesic flow and the integral cohomology ring of complex projective space. The ordinary first heat coefficient then identifies the total scalar curvature except on a Pell sequence of pairs. For those pairs, a clean wave-trace argument, a Krawtchouk estimate, and a mod-two projective-bundle obstruction determine the geodesic return holonomy. A canonical K\"ahler involution recovers a weighted first heat coefficient which is nonzero throughout the exceptional sequence. The Kobayashi--Ochiai theorem and a fixed-class second-heat-coefficient calculation complete the argument.

item.title: Pointed Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory
item.author: Andrei Bud, Richard Haburcak
item.description:
Andrei Bud, Richard Haburcak

Matched: Andrei Bud · math.AG · new

We study the geometry of Hurwitz--Brill--Noether spaces with vanishing conditions at a totally ramified point. Degeneration to a curve with an elliptic tail simplifies the combinatorics of Larson, Larson--Larson--Vogt, and Aggarwal, giving inductive proofs of Aggarwal's results in the one-point setting, and yields an efficient recursion for the algebraic Euler characteristics. Finally, when the expected dimension is negative, we give a numerical criterion ensuring the universal Hurwitz--Brill--Noether locus admits a component of expected relative dimension, generically finite over its image in the Hurwitz space, analogous to the existing results of Pflueger and Teixidor i Bigas for classical Brill--Noether loci.

item.title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
item.author: Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan
item.description:
Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.AG · new

We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang's descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, K\"ahler--Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture.

item.title: The inverse local-relative correspondence and the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation
item.author: Jianjun Fu, Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang
item.description:
Jianjun Fu, Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang

Matched: Shuai Guo · math.AG · new

We prove the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation for the local Gromov--Witten theory of smooth weak del Pezzo surfaces, by identifying its unique formal solution with the inverse of the local-relative correspondence. We construct this inverse through an associative set-partition convolution and establish the identification using Zagier's recursion for the Bloch--Okounkov $n$-point function. The proof applies in all genera and includes non-toric surfaces.

item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

item.title: Uniform asymptotics and the Weil--Petersson constant
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.AG · new

In their celebrated work on the large-genus asymptotic expansion of Weil--Petersson volumes, Mirzakhani and Zograf left open the question of whether the Weil--Petersson constant satisfies $C_{\mathrm{WP}}=\pi^{-1/2}$. We resolve the conjecture affirmatively. Our strategy is to consider a family of spectral curves interpolating between $y=z-4z^3$ and $y=\sin(2\pi z)/(2\pi)$. For each fixed number $n\geq2$ of marked points, we normalize the cusp coefficients using the action integral and the derivative at its first positive zero. We prove that the logarithmic derivatives of these normalized coefficients with respect to the family parameter are $O_n(g^{-1})$, uniformly along the family. The proof combines the descendant recursion, positivity, the dilaton equation, KdV, and coefficient asymptotics for the Painlev\'e I equation.

item.title: From one particle to N particles: uniform transport-information and log-Sobolev inequalities for Coulomb gases on the torus
item.author: A Guillin (LMBP), W Liu (LMBP), B Nectoux (LMBP), L Wu (LMBP)
item.description:
A Guillin (LMBP), W Liu (LMBP), B Nectoux (LMBP), L Wu (LMBP)

Matched: Longting Wu · math.FA, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We study how a functional inequality satisfied by the one-particle conditional distributions of a Gibbs measure, with a constant independent of the positions of the other particles, can be propagated to the whole N -particle system, with a constant independent of N , when the interaction is singular. Our model is the Coulomb gas on the torus T 3 in the mean-field regime. We distinguish two mechanisms. The first one is a dependent tensorization, governed by Dobrushin-Wu interdependence coefficients. It yields uniform Poincar{\'e} and transport-information W 2 I inequalities with fully explicit constants. We explain why this mechanism does not extend to the log-Sobolev inequality: the Zegarlinski-type coefficients, which require pointwise bounds on the interaction, are infinite. The second mechanism is a tensorization with a defect. Using a uniform bound on the partition function due to Duerinckx and Jabin, it yields a uniform log-Sobolev inequality for the Coulomb gas on T 3 at small charge. We identify the assumptions on the interaction under which each mechanism applies. All the results are then extended to the two-dimensional Coulomb gas and to periodic Riesz gases 1/|x|^s , 0 < s $\le$ 1. The extension to d $\ge$ 4 is also discussed.

item.author: Vladimiro Benedetti (LJAD), Simone Billi (CMLS), Nicolas Perrin (CMLS)
item.description:
Vladimiro Benedetti (LJAD), Simone Billi (CMLS), Nicolas Perrin (CMLS)

item.title: Deligne--Faltings Logarithmic Derived Geometry with a View towards Logarithmic GLSM
item.author: Felix Janda, Ruoxi Li
item.description:
Felix Janda, Ruoxi Li

Matched: Felix Janda · math.AG · new

Many perfect obstruction theories and virtual cycles in enumerative geometry are shadows from derived geometry. In this paper, we give a general construction of reduced perfect obstruction theories arising from a geometric reduction of the derived stack $X$ with respect to a $(-1)$-shifted log function $w_\alpha$. Notably, this construction leads to a decomposition of the virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ into the reduced virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{red}}$ and a reduced boundary cycle $[\Delta_X]^\red$. Our construction is motivated by future applications to the moduli stack of UMD logarithmic R-maps in log GLSM \cite{CJR21}. Along the way, we develop logarithmic analogs of several constructions in derived geometry, in particular proving a logarithmic Lagrangian intersection theorem.

item.title: The fifteenth cohomology group of moduli spaces of stable curves
item.author: Amy Bradford, Aitor Iribar L\'opez, Andreas Kretschmer, Hannah Larson
item.description:
Amy Bradford, Aitor Iribar L\'opez, Andreas Kretschmer, Hannah Larson

Matched: Hannah Larson · math.AG · new

The new framework of semi-tautological extensions has allowed for explicit understanding of low-degree odd cohomology groups of moduli spaces of stable curves. Let $S^*_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) \subset H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ denote the semi-tautological extension generated by $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$, that is, the smallest system of subrings of $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ containing $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$ and the tautological subrings, which is also closed under pullbacks along forgetful maps and pushforwards along gluing maps. Recently, it has been shown that $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{11}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ and $H^{13}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{13}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g$ and $n$. Meanwhile, $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}) \neq S_\omega^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n})$ for all $n \geq 15$. Nevertheless, we prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}) = S^{15}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for all $n$. Moreover, we determine all relations in $S_\omega^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g \geq 2$ and give explicit bases for this vector space in terms of decorated graphs. Conditional upon the conjectured dimension of $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,14})$, we also prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n}) = S^{15}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n})$ for all $n$. As an application, we prove $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = RH^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for several new small pairs $(g,n)$.

item.author: David Anderson, Sam Payne
item.description:
David Anderson, Sam Payne

Matched: Sam Payne · math.AG · new

We show that if $\Pi \subseteq G/P$ is a projected Richardson variety, then the degree map $\mathrm{Pic}(\Pi) \to A_1(\Pi)^\vee$ is injective. item.title: Sharp parameter gaps for quantized Mabuchi energies and cscK metrics
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Liangdi Zhang
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Liangdi Zhang

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.DG · new

For polarized manifolds, we show that semistability for the quantized Mabuchi energy at one fixed finite parameter is equivalent to uniform K-stability and to unique existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler (cscK) metrics. We obtain sharp comparisons between quantized Mabuchi slopes at different parameters and with the ordinary Mabuchi slope. In the presence of automorphisms, we give an equivariant criterion using torus twists under the vanishing of the Futaki character. The estimates also hold for finite-energy geodesic rays in compact K\"ahler classes. On a fixed ruled surface with discrete automorphism group, we construct cscK polarizations with unbounded critical parameters. Their ratios to the $\alpha$-invariant are also unbounded.

item.author: Jonas Bergstr\"om, Samir Canning, Dan Petersen, Johannes Schmitt
item.description:
Jonas Bergstr\"om, Samir Canning, Dan Petersen, Johannes Schmitt

Matched: Johannes Schmitt, Samir Canning · math.AG · new

item.description:

item.title: Quantum cohomology, Hitchin systems, and Fourier--Mukai comparison
item.author: Yunfeng Jiang, Hsian-Hua Tseng
item.description:
Yunfeng Jiang, Hsian-Hua Tseng

Matched: Hsian-Hua Tseng · math.AG · new

item.description:
Shuai Guo, Jingyi Xu, Qingsheng Zhang

item.title: Stable ample vector bundles without semipositive Kobayashi curvature
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.DG, math.CV · new

We construct slope-stable ample rank-two vector bundles on every Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb{F}_e$ that admit no smooth strongly pseudoconvex Finsler metric with semipositive Kobayashi curvature. These examples give a negative answer to Kobayashi's problem. The same bundles give counterexamples to the smooth strongly pseudoconvex Finsler formulation of Fulton's problem and to the Hartshorne--Schneider conjecture on the convexity of complements. For $e=1$, these counterexamples have a simply connected Fano base that is not a product.

item.title: From $3$-spin to Negative $r$-spin: Limits of Cohomological Field Theories and Tautological Relations
item.author: Deniz Genlik, Felix Janda
item.description:
Deniz Genlik, Felix Janda

Matched: Felix Janda · math.AG, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We prove that the negative $r$-spin tautological relations of Chidambaram--Garcia-Failde--Giacchetto are a consequence of Pixton's $3$-spin relations, for every $r\ge2$, and deduce that they hold in the tautological Chow ring of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$. In particular, our result for $r=2$ implies that Kazarian--Norbury $K$-relations hold in Chow. The proof factors through two essential parts. The first part shows that the tautological relations arising from Chiodo's class imply the negative $r$-spin relations. This requires an intricate study of limiting behavior of the Givental--Teleman graph contributions. In the second part, we show that the Chiodo relations are a consequence of Pixton's $3$-spin relations as an application of a generalization of Janda's work on tautological relations from CohFTs.
